chapter: On the road, James Brown and the 1956 crash
title: Back and hip unharmed; Lisette's first birthday
summary: Cobb says the fused areas held and only the leg was damaged; he left the hospital the day after his daughter's first birthday and did not work until June 1957.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Well, there was something I wanted to ask you. All that time the back and the hip all stayed right? The original injuries?

I don't have any problem with my back. I don't have any problem today with my hip. Wherever they fused it, that's the strongest part of your body. Won't give an inch. I never had any more problems with my hip, never had any more problems, through that accident and the impact, nothing changed with my back or my hip.
All it did was give me more damage where the leg wouldn't give because the hip didn't give. And I --

-- until June -- I didn't go back to work until June, '57, but I got -- I was discharged from the hospital the day after Lisette's birthday. She was a year and a day old on that picture up there. So they saved her birthday for me. Instead of the 11th we had it on the 12th of January. See that (inaudible) That's her one year birthday. See that cake?
Oh, up there. Isn't that cute? No, I didn't.
